Ordnance 0.4.3. A game update no longer makes the next deploy write old stat tables back, and Chef stays the boot the game actually runs.

## What's new

**Stat plans follow the game you have installed.** Deploy used to apply every stat plan onto the first vanilla copy it saved. After Steam replaced those tables, the next deploy wrote the old ones back over the verified files, and Helldivers 2 crashed on launch. Ordnance now keeps that backup when the live file is still that copy or the last deploy's output, and replaces it only when Steam has put a new table in its place.

**Chef Shared Loader stays above file-swap boots.** A multi-resource loader such as Chef was treated as an ordinary boot script, so file-swap installers got merged and deployed above it. The game then ran that merged script instead of Chef. A loader patch now stays the highest boot, and the other boot scripts stay below it.

**Rename a mod in the library.** The name you type is a display override. Entering the manifest's own name clears it.

**Browser extension 1.0.3.** The Nexus button now reads Ordnance Download, sits in the action bar, and shows up on each file when a mod page lists more than one.

## What Ordnance does

**Import from your current mod manager.** One-click import from HD2 Arsenal and Echelon — plus the older HD2 mod manager, Vortex, and your Downloads folder, with names, on/off state, and options intact.

**Automatic update checking and (optionally) downloading.** Ordnance checks every mod against its source — AyakaMods, GitHub, GameBanana, ModWorkshop, and Nexus Mods — and, when you enable it, downloads and installs the ones it can fetch itself.

**One deploy, everything enabled.** Merge mods and generated stat-plan edits into a single sealed swap and a single boot script. No per-mod loader conflicts.

## Get it

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `Ordnance-0.4.3-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows: no install | `Ordnance-0.4.3-windows-x64-portable.zip` |
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | `Ordnance-0.4.3-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux (Fedora/openSUSE) | `Ordnance-0.4.3-linux-x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux: no install | `Ordnance-0.4.3-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `Ordnance-0.4.3-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

**Browser extension:** `ordnance-extension-chrome-1.0.3.zip` or `ordnance-extension-firefox-1.0.3.zip`. Load it unpacked. The button says Ordnance Download.
